- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast 3–7 days post-spike.  
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher prices in early forecast horizon (days 1–7); apply downward bias correction of 1–3% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.3 → -0.4 → +0.2), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend reversal.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative over last 7 days.
